notes.title: Surprise! A New Year's Eve Update!
notes.notes:
Okay so I just got the 'itch' or whatever a few days ago and improved the game some more. Why not a better time than now, right?

--

[h1]ADDITIONS[/h1]

[list]
[*]New Enemy: Owls! Hoo Hoo HOO saw these coming? Nobody, that's hoo. They like to perch on flagpoles and poop on unsuspecting skeletons named Smitty. Even though they don't technically fly around, they DO count as flying enemies and the Spear will deal critical damage when they're struck.

[*]When you read a secret book or are otherwise given a clue about an Old School mode unlock, it'll not specifically mention that to the player. I saw a few streams of the game lately and the way it was worded before left some wondering if there was some secret Cultist Shop somewhere in Vanilla Mode. Now everyone will know that these are specifically Old School mode unlocks for next time.
[/list]

[h1]CHANGES[/h1]

[list]
[*]I got rid of the pile of rocks in the Plant Zone near the save point. This further opens up some new routes / new items to grab early if you want to. Sequence breaking is the name of the game!

[*]The Red Ring now increases regular / non-magic or elemental weapons' damage by +3 (was +2). To those of you who haven't played the game yet, this is actually a pretty huge change.

[*]The Cactus Rod's magic damage was increased from 2-6 to 3-7. I figure this is kind of hard to get so it might as well have more pop to it.

[*]Izo's Razor's curse to heal the enemy instead of damage them was reduced to 4% (was 10%). This make the weapon a hell of a lot more useful to players, since it's a pretty powerful weapon when the heal doesn't kick in.

[*]The Spear's animation was slightly improved and lengthened, as well as its hit box improved. 

[*]Enemy Meat you get from killing enemies is now worth 2 points of food (was 1).
[/list]

[h1]FIXES[/h1]

None this time!

-----

So since last time we spoke the game has been doing actually pretty well for itself. I do have some more plans on possibly making some new additions to it at a later date, but for now this should be a nice surprise for you returning vets and those who picked up Bone Appetit during the Winter Sale.

Happy New Year's!

-Dave / Del_Duio

notes.title: Surprise! It's a Bone Appetit update.. And a 25% off sale!
notes.notes:
Hello!

This is a free surprise content update for everybody's favorite undead food thief, Smitty. I had been kicking around the notion to go back into Bone Appetit and make some changes and additions for quite a while now, but had been super busy working on (and releasing) my 2nd roguelike Equin 2: The Warren Peace. After that game came out, it left me some time to work on this again. And here we are!

What I've done is gone through many areas and aspects of the game and re-evaluated most everything, tweaking as I went. One focus was making the 2nd battery you find more useful (with the charged bricks). Another was to make magic wands and stuff more viable. BUUUUT without spoiling way too much, I can safely say that any existing fans of the game should love this update, and any on the fence well now there's more stuff you can think about before taking the plunge.


[h1]ADDITIONS[/h1]
[list]
[*]There's now a new red door blocking King Fatass' final area in Old School Mode. In order to get past it, you must kill the other 5 bosses. Merely having the green Master Key is no longer enough. This puts a bit more challenge into Old School Mode, which I admit was kind of easy before to just fly through with some select items.
[*]New rooms! A total of 11, area-wise. These are both regular and secret types. They've been distributed about the map in some interesting ways. Remember that old dead end from before? Maybe there's something new there now!
[*]New weapon: Del Duious. This is an upgraded version of the Sword, with better damage, bonus damage vs bosses, and increased defense when equipped (+15%). You'll need to find the new upgrade statue well to change your sword to this.
[*]New Power-Up: Purple Ring+ (Deals +8 damage with all magic wands)
[*]New side quest: Rescue the teddy bear!
[*]New side quest: Outcast Wizard!
[*]More poor cultist corpses about the place. You gotta' love these guys
[*]The Mace now has holy sparklie doos that come out when you swing it (Old School Mode weapon only, after unlocking through the main game).
[/list]

[h1]CHANGES[/h1]
[list]
[*]Re-arranged some of the existing rooms and made them more.. METROIDVANIA-Y
[*]Baby bats in Hugo's boss fight are now the same color as their mum. Make sense, right??
[*]The Noob Rod's range was extended, damage increased from 1-4 to 1-5
[*]Blue Rod damage was increased from 2-4 to 3-6
[*]Magic Wand damage was increased from 3-10 to 5-10
[*]Mace's damage was increased from 2-5 to 3-7
[*]Cactus Rod's magic shield was made much better and its spin animation slightly slowed down, meaning you'll have a more worthwhile shield up for longer that can block more projectiles
[*]Dagger's crit chance when stabbing from behind increased from 20% to 50%
[*]The Flail's swing speed was increased, meaning maybe now somebody will use it for non rock-breaking stuff
[*]Moved some minor treasures around- potion / apple / banana and etc to fill the new rooms
[*]Slightly improved the furnace fires, graphically
[*]Barbell critical damage increased from +25% to +50%
[*]Adjusted the mini map slightly to reflect some of the new room changes
[/list]

[h1]FIXES[/h1]
[list]
[*]Moved the frog slightly as being in the water sometimes didn't trigger a description of what it did when you picked it up.
[/list]

---

So there you go! As of right now, Bone Appetit is sitting at 43 (46) reviews, the goal is to try and get at least 50, as then it'll go into Steam's next bracket for visibility and therefore hopefully more eyes and potential players in the future. So if you like what you see, please consider leaving a review and helping this solo dev out!

Thanks, and have a great day!
-Dave / Del_Duio

notes.title: DXF Games' new one, "Equin 2: The Warren Peace" Roguelike
notes.notes:
The spirit and brains behind Bone Appetit goes on through another adventure!

I have been hard at work on this thing for over a year, with plans to release it this November. With my own personal experiences of being intimidated by many traditional roguelike control schemes I've put it to good use here: EQ2 is intentionally designed to not need a MENSA card in order to play. Whenever you're on or near something you'd like to interact with, just press the space bar and a menu will pop up with any and every available option you're able to perform- Open a chest, Close a door, Drink from a well (or fill an empty bottle from that well), Enter shops, Melt ice with a torch, etc etc you guys get the idea.

The credo of this game is unofficially "Fight monsters, not the controls!"


[h1]The Story So Far[/h1]

An evil wizard has written a 6000-page book, [i]"The Warren Peace"[/i], which is the longest and most boring book known to man. Sending it to your village, the curious townsfolk started to read it and then PROMPTY BORED THEMSELVES TO DEATH. As the mysterious stranger, you found the book and have vowed to destroy it by returning it FROM WHENCE IT CAME.

[i]"The Warren Peace"[/i] is also an in-game indestructible item, which can be equipped in your off-hand slot and read in combat. This will put your character to sleep for a single round, but enable him to recover stamina. Stamina is used for fighting and many other actions within the game like fishing or digging up graves.


[h1]Main Features[/h1]

[list]
[*] Easy to use controls, which I find to be a rarity for roguelikes
[*] Lovable rabbit warriors, thieves, wizards, and clerics.. to routinely kill all the live long day
[*] Equipped gear visibly shows on your character
[*] Larger visible playing field
[*] Battle enemies in first person combat, or automatically 'bump to kill' weaker ones at high levels
[*] Hundreds of items and gear to find and upgrade
[*] More diverse class skills and this time you can choose what you learn
[*] Travel the world to dispose of the evil book- from swampy temples to arid deserts to underground prisons and more!
[*] A brand new OST featuring real drums, bass, keyboard / synths, and guitars.
[/list]


[h1]WISHLIST TODAY![/h1]

https://steamcommunity.com/app/1630690/

Please stop by and take a GANDER, if you like what you see please by all means Wishlist and Follow! Know anybody who is interested in roguelikes but is easily scared by how complicated they can be to play? Tell them about it too!

notes.title: Very small update- Couple bug fixes
notes.notes:
Hello Bone Appetit fans!

Though the game has been really stable thus far a few days ago it was brought to my attention on the forum that there were a couple of bugs. These were that you could have the necklace during a playthrough after winning the game with the necklace (but you really wouldn't have the necklace). Did that make sense? Well, that's been fixed!

The other bit is that the Barbell- upon picking it up from the chest- was giving Smitty TOO much bonus critical hit damage.. to the tune of +100% vs. the +25% it's supposed to give. Upon saving and quitting (and then restarting) the barbell would revert to the intended crit bonus, but make it seem to the player that something was wrong due to the big damage drop off.

This has also been fixed!

And out there, somewhere, many cats and dogs have also been fixed! Bob Barker would be most pleased indeed. Ah yes, it's been a very tiring week with little sleep I say.

One special note that has nothing to do with games: I found out one of my bass idols, Bones Hillman of Midnight Oil fame, died earlier this week due to cancer. Though I didn't personally know the man, I did have a small e-mail correspondence with him several years back and he seemed like the nicest guy. It's always a bonus when your musical heroes don't turn out to be giant douchebags of course. Aside from Les Claypool (Primus), Bones really inspired me to pick up the bass and try for real. Damn, that was a long time ago.

Earlier this year cancer also took another idol of mine, Rush's Neil Peart. I can't believe he's gone, it doesn't feel real at all. Thank the two of you for all the incredible music you gave to not only myself, but to millions of others throughout the world.

Fuck it all, even Alex Trebek too. I'll take "Crappiest years ever for $400, Alex", wherever you are.

I won't get all sappy or super-preachy, but we're only on this stinking blue ball for a short time so please take a minute or two and look around. Try to appreciate what we have while we have it still. I guess that's all I gotta' say. No more Ghandi-isms from me, promise!

Have a good day, and take care. Maybe my poop jokes will make you smile a bit, hey who knows.
Dave / Del_Duio

notes.title: Game Over... Tune!
notes.notes:
So I was screwing around on my keyboard this morning (the piano one, not the computer one) and came up with a pretty cool chord progression. After being able to not completely screw the changes up, I had a little lead in my head that would go great with it. The short of it is, I wrote this in maybe an hour and just recorded it now... which is now the new Bone Appetit game over tune!

So even though you'll have to die to hear it...

Enjoy!

notes.title: Minor achievement fixes (2)
notes.notes:
Hey guys!

Sorry for the intrusion however there were 2 achievements that didn't activate for some players so I had to fix them and re-upload the build. This will not interfere with your saves of course.

Though these did work before, I had forgotten that I made some last-minute type of item moves and etc to make for a better "Metroidvania Flow". And once that happened, some of the triggers for a couple achievements failed to trigger.

In fact, if you've already technically gotten the achievement it should count as soon as you turn the game on and start playing. So you don't have to do it all over again!

To Bone Appetit's new players: Thank you very much for giving my little game a shot! I encourage you to share interesting / funny screenshots with our growing community as well. 

Have a great weekend!

-Dave / Del_Duio
